dedupe_keys.name: gtfsrouter r package for routing with gtfs data

description: gtfsrouter is an R package that uses General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) data for public transport routing from nominated start and end stations, for extracting isochrones and for computing travel times from any nominated start station to all other stations. It is written in R with C++ through Rcpp and data.table, and its vignettes cover the main functions, transfer tables and travel times. It is developed by Mark Padgham and Marcin Stepniak, with contributions from Alexandra Kapp, under the UrbanAnalyst organisation, with a mirror on Codeberg. Coverage is generic: any GTFS feed. Access: free under the GPL-3 licence from CRAN (version 0.1.4, published 18 June 2025, DOI 10.32614/CRAN.package.gtfsrouter) and GitHub. Caveats: it routes on scheduled timetables only, and the package version is still below 1.0. It supports accessibility and travel time analysis on public transport networks, isochrones for equity studies and before-and-after comparisons of service changes or disruptions, and complements GTFS Kit, UrbanAccess and the GTFS specification catalogued here.
